exposure: Placental location (anterior, posterior, lateral, fundal, low-lying)
outcome: Maternal complications (preeclampsia, eclampsia, premature rupture of membranes)
Neonatal outcomes (birth weight, APGAR scores, NICU admissions, fetal weight)
cohort: The study included 125 pregnant women who underwent ultrasound evaluations during their second and third trimesters.
finding: Lateral placental location was notably associated with higher rates of maternal complications (preeclampsia, eclampsia, premature rupture of membranes) and adverse neonatal outcomes (low birth weight, NICU admissions).
mod_finding: All cases of low-lying placenta resulted in cesarean deliveries.
